concerns.text: T002 is tagged [P] but its own Check says 'run on the T001 subset' — it consumes data/raw/ produced by T001. A consumer-before-producer dependency makes the [P] tag unsafe; either drop [P] from T002 or restrict [P] to T001 only. The 'Execution order' note ('T001 and T002 are parallelizable') repeats the error.

T003 writes per-subject rows to data/results/metrics.csv 'with all fields required by output.schema.yaml', but cohort-level fields (t_statistic, p_value_fdr, cohen_d, significant) are only produced in T005. The producer/consumer chain is ordered correctly, but T003's stated output contract implies fields that have no producer task at T003's position — clarify that T003 emits per-subject fields and T005 augments/merges the statistical fields.

T005's topographic validation consumes data/templates/canonical_mmn.npy produced in T004 — ordering is correct, but T005's description does not state this input dependency explicitly; add 'loaded from data/templates/canonical_mmn.npy (T004)' so the dependency is machine-checkable.
